tasks.title: Same molecular formula, different carbon bonding
tasks.prompt: An unknown hydrocarbon has formula C₄H₈. One student insists that it must be an alkene because open-chain alkenes follow CₙH₂ₙ. Construct two distinct valence-valid connected structures for this formula, at least one without a carbon–carbon double bond. Use the structures to evaluate how far the formula and a positive bromine-water test together support an alkene assignment.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: But-1-ene CH₂=CH–CH₂–CH₃ is an open-chain alkene C₄H₈; cyclobutane is a saturated ring also C₄H₈. Both satisfy typical carbon valence four. Thus the molecular formula alone does not establish a double bond. Bromine-water decolourisation under controlled conditions may support unsaturation but can arise from other reactions/contaminants, and some cyclic compounds can react under other conditions; confirm structural/chemical identity with suitable independent evidence.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Choose open-chain double-bond vs ring model.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate molecular formula to two valid connectivity graphs.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Compare valence and interpret added test.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Formula CnH2n has ring and alkene alternatives.

self_score_proposal.qualification_note: Not independently QRT-adjudicated. Difficulty may be downgraded if task is not intrinsically high demand or if scaffolding reveals the decisive work.

tasks.title: Unknown oxygenated organic substances from incomplete tests
tasks.prompt: Two compounds A and B both have molecular formula C₃H₈O. A shows an alcohol-like oxidation response under selected conditions; B has no such response, and a student states 'B must be a ketone'. Build at least two distinct structures consistent with the formula, identify which common functional-group assignments are impossible from the atom inventory alone, and construct a cautious test sequence that could discriminate propanol isomers from an ether. Explain why no single colour change establishes molecular connectivity.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: C₃H₈O can be propan-1-ol CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, propan-2-ol CH₃CH(OH)CH₃, or methoxyethane CH₃OCH₂CH₃. A ketone such as propanone is C₃H₆O, so 'B must be ketone' contradicts the H count if the given formula is correct. Both propanols can oxidize under appropriate conditions, though products differ; an ether may not give the same response. Confirm the formula, use appropriate functional-group identification including controlled oxidation-product analysis and structural evidence. Separate a negative reaction under one condition from proof of ether identity. This is a model-selection and representation problem, not a one-colour answer key.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Select between two alcohol isomers and an ether under the known formula.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate formula to structural connectivity and reaction constraints.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Integrate oxidation result and H count against ketone claim.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: An intuitive ketone diagnosis contradicts C₃H₈O; negative test is not proof.
